results.title: Mohammed Bin Rashid Aerospace Hub advances construction of Sky Support Complex as completion nears
results.description: Dubai: Mohammed Bin Rashid Aerospace Hub (MBRAH), the aerospace platform of Dubai South, has announced that construction of its Sky Support Complex remains on schedule for completion by the end of the third quarter of 2026. The milestone marks further progress in MBRAH's efforts to expand infrastructure and support the growing requirements of the aerospace sector. Located within the Aerospace Supply Chain Zone, the Sky Support Complex is a landside facility covering 16,661 square metres and comprising 14 premium units designed for aviation-related businesses. Upon completion, the complex will offer flexible warehouse, office and commercial spaces, along with dedicated landside access and seamless connectivity to Al Maktoum International Airport and the wider Dubai South ecosystem. The facility is situated within a bonded free zone, providing benefits including 100% foreign ownership, advanced infrastructure and a business-friendly operating environment tailored to the aviation industry. Tahnoon Saif, Chief Executive Officer of MBRAH, said the development reflects the organisation's commitment to supporting the evolving needs of the aviation sector. "The progress achieved at the Sky Support Complex reflects our continued commitment to developing facilities that support the evolving needs of the aviation industry," he said. "As demand for specialised aerospace facilities continues to grow, we remain focused on delivering premium developments that enable businesses to expand, enhance operational efficiency and benefit from Dubai's world-class aviation ecosystem." The Sky Support Complex forms part of MBRAH's broader strategy to strengthen Dubai's position as a leading global aviation and aerospace hub by providing specialised infrastructure for businesses operating across the sector.

results.title: Flipster Secures VARA Exchange License to Launch Regulated Crypto Trading in UAE
results.description: Flipster, an international cryptocurrency trading platform, has obtained a full operational Exchange license (License No. VL/26/07/002) from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) through its regional entity, Flipster FZE. The approval allows the company to begin offering regulated virtual asset services in the UAE and represents a major milestone in Flipster's international growth strategy. Under the newly granted license, Flipster FZE can onboard customers in the United Arab Emirates, with plans to gradually extend its regulated services to a wider global audience. The platform also provides access to real-world asset perpetuals in eligible jurisdictions, enabling traders to gain exposure to both digital assets and traditional financial markets. Initially, Flipster's regulated offerings will center on spot trading, laying the groundwork for a broader suite of compliant products. Receiving the operational license signifies Flipster's progression from obtaining in-principle approval and meeting regulatory requirements to becoming a fully authorized exchange under VARA's regulatory framework. VARA is widely regarded as one of the world's leading authorities for the oversight of virtual assets, known for its comprehensive approach to digital asset regulation. By operating within VARA's regulatory framework, Flipster aims to deliver a secure, transparent, and compliant trading experience. The platform's operations are supported by stringent requirements governing custody, corporate governance, and regulatory compliance, reinforcing its commitment to protecting users while ensuring dependable access to digital asset markets. The licensing achievement also underscores Flipster's dedication to maintaining high standards of regulatory compliance in global financial markets. The company views effective regulation as a key driver of long-term trust and recognizes VARA's framework for successfully balancing innovation with strong investor safeguards. Flipster announced its expansion into the Middle East in May 2025 with the appointment of Benjamin Grolimund as General Manager of Flipster FZE. Securing the full operational license marks the next stage of this regional strategy, enabling the company to move beyond market entry and begin delivering fully regulated virtual asset services within one of the world's most advanced digital asset ecosystems.

results.title: Industry players form alliance to advocate for secure use of open AI tools, amid increased scrutiny over China’s role
results.description: Several tech firms led by NVIDIA have formed the Open Secure AI Alliance, a new coalition emphasizing the importance of open source software in the “global economy,” following a push by big companies and startups urging government officials to move away from imposing restrictions on open-weight AI models. “Just as open source created a shared foundation for software, the United States and its partners now face a choice in AI security: whether the defenses that protect our infrastructure will sit inside a few opaque systems or be built on open models, harnesses and tools that any defender can study, adapt and deploy,” according to a July 27 blog post from NVIDIA announcing the new alliance. The post argues, “The world needs both closed and open models.” Open models are particularly important for cybersecurity “because they democratize defensive capabilities, increase transparency for defenders, enable cyber defense while protecting data, and complement frontier closed models with customizable, localized controls,” the post says. In addition, the post says, “Open source enables massively distributed community-driven and self-controlled defense – with no single point of failure.” The post highlights the Hugging Face security incident , arguing that it “delivered a clear reminder: cyber defenders need open, frontier agentic systems for self-defense.” The incident involved an OpenAI model gaining unauthorized access to the Hugging Face platform as part of a performance evaluation. “When closed AI tools — unable to distinguish attackers from defenders — blocked essential forensic analysis, Hugging Face ran the open-weight GLM 5.2 model on its own infrastructure to analyze more than 17,000 actions and contain the intrusion,” the post says. The alliance has several tech firms including Cisco, Cloudera, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, IBM, Microsoft, NetApp, Palantir. Palo Alto Networks, Red Hat and Salesforce. Hugging Face is also part of the alliance, alongside the Linux Foundation, Capital One, Space X, TrendAI and DoorDash. Several tech firms signed a July 24 open letter on the importance of “Open Weights and American AI leadership” and nearly 200 startup companies have joined forces to urge the Trump administration to not cut off access to open-weight AI models developed in China. On June 25, several leading AI and tech firms signed onto a Linux Foundation project, known as Akrites , (/node/18196) to address vulnerabilities in open source software and combine resources to address them. The alliance post says, “Cybersecurity is among the top three beneficiaries of open source software. The Open Secure AI Alliance — building on the leadership of the Linux Foundation’s Akrites initiative and OpenSSF community work — will work to remediate and disclose vulnerabilities using open technologies.” The post contains a call to action for policymakers and regulators. It says, “As policymakers and regulators grapple with AI safety, it will be crucial to recognize open models, harnesses and security tooling as defensive assets, not liabilities, in AI and cybersecurity policy. Blanket restrictions on open frontier AI systems would weaken defensive capacity and risk concentrating power, dependence and vulnerability in a few closed providers.” The alliance argues, “Companies and governments should invest in shared open infrastructure for AI defense — datasets, evaluation frameworks, attack simulators and red-teaming tools — much as past generations invested in open source software.” -- Sara Friedman (sfriedman@iwpnews.com) Article Type: Daily News Sara Friedman tags: AI Weight: -20
